title: The Hand That Plays in Dissonance
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector, Detective Takagi) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. Per the 2026-08 batch-8+ scoping change, temporal fields (order/temporal_frame/years_before_present) are omitted entirely -- not required going forward. Discrepancies found vs. the old lower-fidelity `cases/ep544_the_hand_that_plays_in_dissonance.json`: (1) the old file's event e1 claimed the murder happened 'in the elevator hall' -- the transcript instead establishes the real crime scene as the 8th floor, near a children's-drawing display (crayon smear on the victim's shoulder matches a partially rubbed-off drawing there); the green room was only where the body was staged/discovered. (2) the old file's stated motive ('rage -- she laughed at him during a confrontation') is not supported anywhere in the transcript; the actual motive given on-screen is that Nakamura, the band's leader, feared the band (his 'life') would collapse once Yukiko and Aoki left to join a new label-backed band recruited by Thomas Records producer Sakamoto. (3) the old file had no red-herring motives or relationships at all (flat 'knows' edges only) despite the transcript containing a full argument scene where Nishimoto, Aoki, Risako and Sakamoto accuse each other over jealousy/affair/key-access angles -- these are now represented as their own has_motive_against edges. Murderer identity (Nakamura Yuusuke) itself matches the old file. case_type: murder.

Only Nakamura helped staff move the instruments into the green room, giving him sole opportunity to smuggle the drum case in
Crayon on the victim's shoulder matches a rubbed-off drawing on the 8th floor, not anything in the green room -- the real scene was the 8th floor
Rectangular pressure mark on the victim's shin matches the drum case's internal handle fitting, proving she was carried inside it
